title: Write the adoption scan
prompt:
Write `measureAdoption(root)` so it scans the `<button>` elements inside `root` (a document or any element) and returns `{ total, system, percent }`:

- `total`: the number of `<button>` elements,
- `system`: how many have `data-nw-component="Button"`, the marker only the real component renders (the `nw-button` class doesn't count; teams copied it),
- `percent`: `system / total` as a whole number rounded with `Math.round`, or `0` when there are no buttons.

Then write the page result into `#report` as `4 of 8 buttons use Northwind UI (50%)`, using your computed numbers.
hints: `[...root.querySelectorAll('button')]` gives you an array of every button inside `root`.
Build the report with a template literal: `${result.system} of ${result.total} buttons use Northwind UI (${result.percent}%)`.
explanation: Counting by the data attribute measures what you actually care about: elements rendered by the real system component. Counting the `nw-button` class would report 6 of 8 (75%) here, because two teams copied the class into their own buttons, and you'd never find out that those forks exist. Accepting any `root` lets the same function report per page section or per team area, and computing on demand means the numbers stay right as the page changes.

checks.ignores-copies: Copied `nw-button` classes don't count as adoption
checks.live: The count updates when a system button is added to the page
